observation.visible_scene: A dark, overcast outdoor scene on a flat open field (resembling a runway or airfield) bordered by a distant line of bare, leafless trees. Centered in the frame is a large, already-formed explosion cloud: finger-like plumes of dark gray/black smoke rising upward, with a dense billowing mass of pale gray-white smoke at the base. A small dark debris fragment is visible in the upper-right sky. The camera is static; the horizon and tree line remain fixed throughout.
visible_changes: The explosion is already in progress at the start of the segment; no ignition or onset is shown.

Over time, orange-yellow flames emerge within the cloud (first faint flecks around t=0.64s, then a distinct glowing core by t=1.0-1.5s) and progressively intensify, illuminating the smoke from within.
The fireball/flame region grows larger and brighter toward the end of the segment (t=2.5-3.2s), with bright combustion spreading across the central and right portions of the cloud.
The dark smoke column continues to rise, billow, and deform upward, its plumes shifting shape while the overall cloud stays centered in roughly the same horizontal position.
The white/gray base cloud slowly expands and churns but remains near ground level.

A small dark object in the upper-right sky drifts upward and to the right across the frames (from mid-upper-right toward the top-right edge), consistent with a flying debris fragment, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or trigger of the explosion and what material is burning are not shown.
The initial detonation/impact and the eventual dissipation or aftermath of the fireball lie outside this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the pale base cloud is steam, condensed vapor, or smoke is not determinable.
The identity and trajectory of the small flying object (debris vs. bird) is uncertain.
The exact fuel or substance producing the flames is unknown.
